NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed an appeal filed by the Andhra Pradesh government challenging an order of the high court which struck down two government orders providing 34 per cent reservation for backward classes in local body elections.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said the Andhra Pradesh High Court passed a reasonable order.The high court on October 1 had struck down two government orders, observing that the quota was against Supreme Court guidelines that total reservation should not exceed 50 per cent.The high court had directed the state government and the State Election Commission to begin the election process within six weeks.On August 18, Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu had announced the 34 per cent quota for backward classes in local body polls."We have taken this decision as part of the coalition government's political principle and NDA's promise. NEW DELHI: Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) on Friday dismissed Professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, who was accused of sexual harassment by at least 10 students, following an inquiry by the university's Internal Committee (IC).An order issued by JNU on October 9 said the committee had investigated the allegations against Akoijam, who taught at the Centre for the Study of Social Systems under the School of Social Sciences. Article Title: Deeply Offensive: Government rebuts Vance’s indentured servants remark
Article Text:
The ministry also cautioned in its response that the steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries.

Following a long period of strained India-US ties, the gloves came off finally as India hit out at US Vice President JD Vance for labelling H-1B visa holders and foreign tech professionals as foreign indentured servants - a characterisation New Delhi slammed as deeply offensive and unwarranted.The scathing response followed the US announcement about the suspension of many tech companies, including several from India, from the PERM Green Card programme. Vance had reinforced the announcement by declaring that American workers cannot be laid off and then replaced with foreign indentured servants. He also insisted that only top-tier, elite foreign talent that's not available domestically should be brought in.The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) countered Vance's comments as it said in a formal statement that such descriptions were unwarranted and ignored the fact that Indian professionals in the US are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem."Indeed, the history of the United States itself has been shaped by generations of immigrants whose labour, enterprise and innovation have contributed to its growth and prosperity.Resorting to terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations is deeply offensive," said the ministry, adding it will continue to follow developments related to the issue.The unusually blunt pushback suggests India's patience is wearing thin after a series of bilateral setbacks, ranging from trade and tariffs, immigration and talent mobility to India's ties with Russia and Washington's Pakistan outreach. External affairs minister S Jaishankar had recently warned that the US' growing ties with Pakistan would hurt the India-US relationship.The ministry also cautioned in its response that the steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries. It said talent mobility adds value to both economies, creating opportunities for Indians and helping US companies equally with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation, besides creating shareholder wealth in the US."This is therefore an area of tremendous mutual benefit for the two countries and our expectation is that all stakeholders in this process can appreciate this fact," said the Indian government.However, the statement also took note of the fact that PERM is distinct from the H-1B visa programme. "The suspension of PERM applications does not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of H-1B visa holders and their dependents, though there could be some impact on the permanent-residency/Green Card process of eligible employees of the affected companies," said the ministry.While the America First signalling through the announcement seems designed for an electoral boost in the upcoming mid-term polls, it's unlikely to help the already rocky state of India-US ties. The timing is also problematic as it creates poor optics for PM Narendra Modi's visit to the US in December for the G20 summit. It also comes just ahead of Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to India this month, during which India will look to raise its concerns related to the issue.The US announcement is the latest flashpoint in ties after the US Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 (SRIA), a new law that empowers the president to impose up to 100 percent tariffs on countries importing Russian oil. Modi had raised India's anxieties about that issue in a phone call with President Donald Trump late last month.
Article Summary: India hit out at US Vice President JD Vance for labelling H-1B visa holders and foreign tech professionals as foreign indentured servants. New Delhi slammed characterisation as deeply offensive and unwarranted. The scathing response followed the US announcement about the suspension of many tech companies, including several from India.

Article Title: Patrón co-founder John Paul DeJoria turned a 96-acre Texas ranch into a home for more than 120 exotic animals; when it sold for $6.93 million, the buyer inherited the herd and a 2,700-square-foot unde
Article Text:
The ranch, known as “Patrón de Paz,” was located in Dripping Springs, about 40 minutes west of Austin.

A ranch that came with more than a house

The main residence measured 7,540 square feet and had four bedrooms and six bathrooms.

The underground shelter

The animals were part of the deal

Why DeJoria sold the ranch

DeJoria co-founded Patrón Spirits Company in 1989.

A 96-acre Texas ranch once owned by Patrón Tequila co-founder John Paul DeJoria came with an unusual combination of luxury, wildlife and an underground shelter. More than 120 exotic African animals lived on the property, while the estate also had a 7,540-square-foot main house, two barns, a stocked pond, a pecan orchard and a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter. The ranch, known as “Patrón de Paz,” was located in Dripping Springs, about 40 minutes west of Austin, and stretched along 2,600 feet of Fitzhugh Creek. According to the Houston Chronicle, the property was listed for $7.495 million in 2016 after initially being put on the market for $7.99 million. It eventually sold for $6.93 million. As reported by ABC13 Houston, television director Jonathan Nowzaradan is the buyer of the ranch.The property was not simply a large Texas home. Its listing described it as an exotic-animal ranch, and the buyer was set to inherit more than 120 exotic African animals. According to the Houston Chronicle, the animals were part of the property when it was listed. The ranch included two barns, each with attached guest quarters, along with a stocked pond and a pecan orchard. As reported by The San Antonio Express-News, the animals included more than 120 exotic species and that the property was being sold with the animals and its furnishings.The estate itself covered 96 acres and overlooked Fitzhugh Creek, which feeds from Barton Creek. The main residence measured 7,540 square feet and had four bedrooms and six bathrooms. It featured wood-beamed ceilings, hardwood floors, partial stone walls and a large gourmet kitchen with a commercial-grade stove. Outside, there was a pool and spa, an outdoor kitchen and a wide porch overlooking the surrounding Hill Country.One of the property's more unusual features was underground. As reported by The San Antonio Express-News, the ranch included a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter. The Austin Business Journal also described the property as having a “2,700-square underground shelter.” So, when the ranch changed hands, the buyer was getting far more than a luxury residence. The property came with its land, buildings, underground shelter and a large collection of exotic animals.The exotic animals were among the details that made the ranch unusual in the first place. As reported by The Houston Chronicle, the new owner would inherit more than 120 exotic African animals. The ranch was a 96-acre property with a spa pool, limestone walls and the animals. The animals included species such as gazelles, wildebeest and antelopes.DeJoria, best known for co-founding John Paul Mitchell Systems and Patrón Spirits Company, had owned Patrón de Paz since 2008, as reported by the San Antonio Express-News. Realtor Dave Murray said DeJoria's primary residence was near Lake Austin and that he had decided to sell the Dripping Springs ranch. Murray also said DeJoria owned several other homes around the world and was selling four estates at the time. DeJoria co-founded John Paul Mitchell Systems with hairdresser Paul Mitchell in 1980 and later co-founded Patrón Spirits Company in 1989. The ranch's sale meant that its next owner did not simply acquire a large piece of Texas Hill Country property. The $6.93 million deal also brought with it a ready-made exotic-animal ranch, two barns, a creekside estate, a stocked pond and a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter.
Article Summary: The ranch, known as ‘Patrón de Paz,’ was located in Dripping Springs, about 40 minutes west of Austin. The main residence measured 7,540 square feet and had four bedrooms and six bathrooms. The ranch included two barns, a stocked pond, a pecan orchard and a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter. The new owner would inherit more than 120 exotic African animals.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday slammed US vice-president JD Vance over his description of H-1B visa workers as "indentured servants", calling his remarks "unwarranted" and "deeply offensive".In a statement, responding to Vance’s comments, the ministry said, "We have also seen some comments in this context by the US Vice President. We believe that such descriptions are unwarranted and ignore the fact that Indian professionals in the United States are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem."The MEA also highlighted the contribution of immigrants to the US economy, saying, "Indeed, the history of the United States itself has been shaped by generations of immigrants whose labour, enterprise and innovation have contributed to its growth and prosperity.""Resorting to terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations is deeply offensive," it added.Vance made the remarks while addressing a news conference on visa fraud, alleging that companies bring in foreign workers at lower wages while laying off American employees.“If you are working as an H-1B visa in the United States of America, you’re earning $20,000 less than an American citizen hired in the same position.If you were brought in by one of these foreign outsourcing firms, you’re making $48,000 less than an American citizen in a similar position," Vance said."So, I’m sure that everybody here understands the game that is being played. You bring in indentured servants from outside the country, you lay off American workers and, if you’re a corporation, you make a ton of money by under cutting the wages of American workers, replacing them with people who frankly shouldn’t be in the United States of America to begin with,” he added.The MEA said that it was aware of the US department of labor’s decision concerning the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) programme for certain companies."It should also be clear that talent mobility adds value to both economies. While it creates opportunities for Indians, it equally helps US companies with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation, besides creating shareholder wealth in the US," the statement said."This is therefore an area of tremendous mutual benefit for the two countries and our expectation is that all stakeholders in this process can appreciate this fact. The steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries,” it added.The MEA also clarified that PERM is separate from the H-1B visa programme. It said the suspension of PERM applications does not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of visa holders and their dependents, although it could affect the green card process for eligible employees of the companies concerned.“We continue to follow developments around this issue,” the ministry added.The MEA’s response came a day after the Trump administration suspended eight companies, TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Cognizant, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe, from participating in the PERM programme.The US administration’s move is part of a broader crackdown on skilled-worker immigration. US officials have alleged that companies have used the system at the expense of American workers.The US department of labor said it would stop accepting and processing new and pending PERM applications involving the affected companies.PERM is an important step in the employment-based green card process. Employers generally need labour certification from the US department of labor before sponsoring eligible foreign workers for permanent residence.The process requires employers to establish that there are not enough qualified, willing and available US workers for a position and that hiring a foreign worker will not adversely affect wages and working conditions.
Article Summary: US vice-president JD Vance described H-1B visa workers as 'indentured servants' The ministry of external affairs called his remarks "unwarranted" and "deeply offensive" Vance made the remarks while addressing a news conference on visa fraud.

Article Title: ‘Lot of talk about one company’: Centre tells satcom firms to meet security norms amid Musk's Starlink row
Article Text:
File photo: Union telecom minister Jyotiraditya Scindia, Elon Musk and Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: Communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia on Friday said satellite communication (satcom) companies can begin operations in India only after individually meeting the required security conditions and milestones, stressing that three companies have received licences despite the focus on Elon Musk ’s Starlink. He also took a dig at Congress for their response to Musk's statements.“There is a lot of conversation about one specific company, but three companies have got satcom licences,” Scindia said, underlining that each operator must fulfil the required conditions before it can start services.Scindia’s remarks come amid a row between Musk and the Indian government over the delay in Starlink’s commercial launch in the country. The SpaceX chief had alleged that “certain oligarchs” were blocking the company to protect their “monopolistic chokehold” on the Indian market, without initially naming anyone.The government rejected the allegation, describing India’s regulatory framework for satellite communication services as “fair and non-discriminatory”. It said security assessments were underway for all three licensed operators and that each could move to the next stage of seeking spectrum assignment once the process was completed. The government called suggestions of discriminatory treatment “baseless and misconceived”.Minister of state for communications Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani said the security clearance issue was pending with the ministry of home affairs and had “nothing to do with one company”.Scindia also took a swipe at Congress saying that the party had earlier objected to a particular person getting a licence but was now aligned with the same person in questioning why the licence had not been granted. He accused the party of not knowing whether it was “going left or right”.The remarks come after Musk stepped up his criticism on Thursday, saying Starlink was licensed in more than 165 countries and had spent five years complying with Indian government requirements. He questioned why the company was still awaiting approval and asked whether industrialist Mukesh Ambani was the “real boss of India”.Leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi responded to Musk on X, writing: “Welcome to India, Elon. Wait till you discover the other guy.”Musk replied: “Thank you, Rahul. This is indeed troubling.”
Article Summary: Communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said three companies have received licences. He also took a dig at Congress for their response to Elon Musk's statements. Scinda’s remarks come amid a row between Musk and the Indian government over the delay in Starlink's commercial launch.

Article Title: Railways cancel several Mail/Express trains reaching New Delhi, Hazrat Nizamuddin on October 10
Article Text:
On October 10, all Mail and Express trains arriving at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin will be canceled

Railway's statement

NEW DELHI: Indian Railways has ordered the cancellation of several Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4am and 2pm on October 10, citing the possibility of severe road traffic congestion around the two stations.According to a railway order issued on October 9, several Mail and Express trains departing from their originating stations after 2pm on Friday and scheduled to reach New Delhi or Hazrat Nizamuddin between 4am and 2pm on Saturday will be cancelled at source.The order, issued by the railway department's coaching directorate, said the decision was taken in view of anticipated severe traffic congestion in the areas surrounding the two stations.The move comes amid protests against the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), though railway officials have not confirmed whether the cancellations are linked to the demonstrations.
Article Summary: Indian Railways has ordered the cancellation of several Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin. The decision was taken in view of anticipated severe traffic congestion in the areas surrounding the two stations. Move comes amid protests against the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), though railway officials have not confirmed whether the cancellations are linked to the demonstrations.

Article Title: 'Jantar Mantar a designated site to protest, police permission not needed': Abhijeet Dipke on October 10 stir
Article Text:

Dipke invokes Article 19

NEW DELHI: A day ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed protest in Delhi, its founder Abhijeet Dipke on Friday hit out at the authorities over restrictions on public transport, saying the government should shut down the entire country if it was scared of the youth.The CJP has called for a demonstration at Jantar Mantar on Saturday to demand the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, alleging large-scale irregularities in the Election Commission’s special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The Railway Board on Friday cancelled certain mail and express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4am and 2pm on October 10. Meanwhile, the Delhi Police urged the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) to shut 57 metro stations to prevent the movement of youths expected to join the protest.Speaking to reporters, Dipke questioned the restrictions and maintained that government permission was not required to protest at Jantar Mantar, a designated protest site.Questioning the measures taken ahead of the demonstration, Dipke said, "What is this fear? Why are you this scared? You are scared of the youth in the country. You shut down trains, you shut down metro, what should one do?""Shut down the entire country if you are scared of the youth," he said.The Delhi Police, however, denied permission for the CJP’s proposed protest at Jantar Mantar, citing short notice, past non-compliance with directions and concerns over public safety, law and order, and traffic regulation.Dipke also questioned the inconvenience caused to commuters, arguing that restrictions on public transport and roads would themselves create difficulties for ordinary people."Is Delhi a property of Narendra Modi or Amit Shah? Is this their ancestral property? Is this their paternal property? On one hand, you say that due to the protest, people are facing inconvenience, and on the other hand, you shut down all the metro, you shut down all the railways, you block all the roads. Now, won't there be inconvenience for people?" he said.Dipke said CJP activists were prepared to face detention or arrest over the planned demonstration."How many people will they detain? Arrest me, detain me! Saurabh is ready, Ashutosh is ready. Arrest me, detain me!" he said.Questioning the need for police permission, Dipke invoked Article 19 of the Constitution, which guarantees certain freedoms, including the right to assemble peacefully, subject to constitutional restrictions. He argued that Jantar Mantar was a designated site for protests."Did Gyanesh Kumar take permission? Before deleting 13 crore votes, did Gyanesh Kumar take permission? The Supreme Court didn't even give approval for the Form 6 modification. So, when Gyanesh Kumar, without telling anyone, without asking anyone, deletes 13 crore votes, then to protest against him, the constitutional right we have according to Article 19, what is the need for permission?" he said.Dipke also questioned the Delhi Police’s requirement that applications to hold protests at Jantar Mantar be submitted at least 10 days in advance, linking the rule to the restrictions imposed ahead of Saturday’s planned demonstration.The CJP’s proposed protest centres on its allegations of irregularities in the SIR exercise.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke hits out at authorities over restrictions on public transport. CJP has called for a demonstration at Jantar Mantar on Saturday to demand the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. NEW DELHI: SpaceX CEO and the world's richest man Elon Musk on Thursday went on a rant explaining how the Starlink's satellite internet services will help the "least served" in India. Musk had just a day earlier alleged that his telecom firm was facing regulatory hurdles in India due to "oligarchs", a claim which was strongly rejected by the Indian government.The SpaceX chief then launched a tweet blitz posting about thrice in just a span of 10 minutes."Starlink will help the least-served in India," he said in a post at 6:18pm.He followed it up with another post at 6:25pm, writing, "Starlink provides Internet connectivity to the least-served, enabling self-education and prosperity by giving people access to sell their products worldwide!"Three minutes later, Elon posted again: "People who oppose @Starlink hurt only the least-served. The wealthy or those living in large cities already have good Internet, so they don’t understand."Musk's comments come as a Starlink delegation is attending the India Mobile Congress organised in the national captial.Musk's claim about Starlink serving the "least-served" in India is somewhat ironic, as India already ranks among the countries with the lowest internet charges in the world."The last decade was about scalability, penetration, affordability.We have discussed many times of how voice prices have crashed, data prices have lowered by almost 97%, which has led to greater penetration," information & technology minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said on Thursday.On the other hand, Starlink will reportedly cost Rs 8,600 per month, with an additional Rs 34,000 one-time hardware charge."Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are … This is a crime against the people of India!" Musk said in a post on Wednesday.The telecom ministry rejected Musk's claim stating, "Security assessment as part of this process is currently under way in respect of all three licensees""The Department of Telecom has issued licences to all satcom companies as well as provisional spectrum. Now the issue is pending with MHA for security clearance. As soon as it is cleared, they will get it. It has nothing to do with one company," minister of state for communications Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani told reporters on the sidelines of the India Mobile Congress.READ ALSO: 'Remain alert, stay indoors': India issues advisory for citizens in Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks The logic behind Starlink is simple: Get internet to places where conventional networks are difficult or too expensive to reach. But Elon Musk’s satellite internet service has increasingly become much more than a tool for connectivity. Its growing use in war zones, conflict areas and during internet shutdowns has turned Starlink into a strategic technology and raised questions over who controls access to it.Critics have raised concerns about the company’s links with US intelligence and military agencies, arguing that a privately controlled satellite network could have implications for national security and sovereignty.Starlink uses thousands of small satellites in low-Earth orbit, around 550km above the planet. Unlike traditional communications satellites positioned around 36,000km away, these satellites can transmit data with lower latency. Users connect through a small receiver with an electronically controlled antenna, which automatically links with satellites passing overhead. The satellites can also transfer data between themselves using laser links.A 2024 report by the Kutniti Foundation, had described Starlink as “a wolf in sheep’s clothing”. The foundation argued that Starlink’s global satellite network gives it capabilities that go beyond conventional telecom services and could create strategic concerns for countries such as India.Furthermore, the satellites also raise security questions. Satellites travel at roughly 11,000 km/h to 28,000 km/h orbiting the earth and can also be used to monitor activity inside the territory of a country.
Article Summary: SpaceX CEO and the world's richest man Elon Musk on Thursday went on a rant explaining how the Starlink's satellite internet services will help the "least served" in India. Musk had just a day earlier alleged that his telecom firm was facing regulatory hurdles in India due to "oligarchs", a claim which was strongly rejected by the Indian government. Critics have raised concerns about the company's links with US intelligence and military agencies.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday said the US government's decision to suspend several technology companies from the employment-based green card programme would not, by itself, affect existing H-1B visas or the status of visa holders and their dependents.The ministry said the suspension of applications under the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme could, however, affect the permanent residency process for eligible employees of the companies concerned.“We are aware of the US Department of Labour’s decision concerning the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme for certain companies. It should be noted that PERM is distinct from the H-1B visa programme,” the MEA said in a statement.“The suspension of PERM applications does not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of H-1B visa holders and their dependents, though there could be some impact on the permanent-residency/Green Card process of eligible employees of the affected companies,” it added.The ministry also emphasised the economic benefits of skilled talent moving between India and the US, saying the latest measures did not advance the shared ambitions of the two countries.“It should also be clear that talent mobility adds value to both economies. While it creates opportunities for Indians, it equally helps US companies with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation, besides creating shareholder wealth in the US,” the MEA said.“This is therefore an area of tremendous mutual benefit for the two countries and our expectation is that all stakeholders in this process can appreciate this fact. The steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries,” it added.The US department of labour has suspended Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini from the PERM programme. The department said it would not accept new applications from the affected companies or process their pending applications amid multiple active federal investigations.US labour secretary Keith Sonderling said the companies had collectively sought millions of foreign workers and received hundreds of thousands of approvals under employment-based immigration programmes.“Since 2009, just these companies alone have requested almost 3 million foreign workers. They received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labour certifications. That's hundreds of thousands of jobs that were taken from American workers,” Sonderling said.The administration has alleged that companies misused employment-based immigration programmes to replace American workers with foreign employees. These are allegations made by US officials; the announcement cited ongoing investigations.PERM is a labour-certification process that allows an eligible US employer to sponsor a foreign worker for employment-based permanent residency, commonly known as a green card. Before certifying an application, the US department of labour must establish that there are not enough qualified and available American workers for the job and that employing the foreign worker would not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed US workers.The H-1B programme, by contrast, allows US employers to hire skilled foreign workers temporarily for specialised occupations. The PERM suspension does not automatically cancel existing H-1B visas, but it could disrupt a route to permanent residency for employees whose employers are sponsoring them through the programme.The move comes amid a wider crackdown by the Trump administration on skilled foreign labour. A day before the announcement, the US department of homeland security proposed new fees for F-1 international students seeking to participate in Optional Practical Training (OPT), describing the measure as an effort to protect American workers and strengthen the integrity of the immigration system.
Article Summary: The US government has suspended several technology companies from the employment-based green card programme. The move comes amid a wider crackdown by the Trump administration on skilled foreign labour. Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini have been suspended.

NEW DELHI: Generative AI has begun cutting into entry-level white-collar hiring in India even as the demand for wo-rkers with AI skills grows, signalling a labour market where some junior roles may disa-ppear while new occupations emerge, World Bank has said.In 'The World Development Report 2026: The Promise of Artificial Intelligence', it said GenAI reduced monthly job postings in India for white-collar occupations most amenable to AI and least complementary to it, with entry-level workers disproportionately affected.Across South Asia, job postings by firms declined 1.6% after ChatGPT's launch in Nov 2022, with a larger impact on multinational affiliates and suppliers linked to global value chains. Among the most exposed white-collar occupations where AI offers ready substitutes, monthly job listings fell by about 20%.Gaurav Nayyar, who led the World Bank team, told TOI the impact would not be uniformly negative. Some occupations in IT and knowledge-intensive services can be automated, he said, while other entry-level jobs would continue to grow and be complemented by AI. Roles like pro-mpt engineers and AI ethics specialists are also emerging.The "critical" part, Nayyar said, was for Indian IT businesses and higher education institutions to impart skills that allow workers to "pivot and adapt" as demands change. He cautioned against excessive specialisation, noting that coding, once seen as a lucrative standalone skill, became one of AI's early automation use cases. He argued for broad-based STEM education, engineering and scientific capacity that lets workers move across occupations.In the first half of 2025, AI-skill vacancies were over five times more common in high-income economies than middle-income ones, but India was among the leading middle-income countries.

Suresh Garimella is the President of the University of Arizona and a distinguished professor in the department of mechanical and aerospace engineering. Focused on building a strong, aligned leadership team and ensuring long-term financial health for the institution, Garimella has consistently championed student access and affordability.Previously President of the University of Vermont, as well as the Goodson Distinguished Professor of mechanical engineering and executive vice president for research and partnerships at Purdue University, he earned his bachelor’s degree from the Indian Institute of Technology Madras before moving to the US. A highly cited scholar, Dr. Garimella was appointed to the newly established office of science advisory committee for the US Department of Energy earlier this year.In an exclusive interview with Ishani Duttagupta, he discusses his deep connection with the global IIT alumni network, the contribution of Indian students to his university, and more. Edited excerpts:Every leader and every university faces moments that test their resilience, but I have found that the most effective leaders remain focused on a clearly articulated mission while bringing people together around a shared vision for the future.Public higher education is changing rapidly. Universities are being asked to prepare students for career paths that are continually and rapidly evolving, accelerate research that addresses society's most pressing challenges and demonstrate their value to the communities they serve. Meeting those expectations requires both disciplined decision-making and the ability to unite people around a common purpose. At the University of Arizona, that has meant making difficult decisions while keeping our eyes firmly on the future. We have strengthened our financial foundation, brought greater focus and discipline to our priorities and positioned the university to build on its considerable strengths. I believe leadership is ultimately about creating the conditions for talented people to succeed. When people understand where an institution is going, how their work contributes and what success looks like, remarkable things become possible.India continues to be one of the University of Arizona’s most important international partners, and Indian students make extraordinary contributions to our campus community through their scholarship, research and leadership. Like at many universities, international enrolment naturally fluctuates in response to global conditions, but our long-term commitment to India remains strong. We continue to explore and secure partnerships with Indian institutions and industry, especially building on areas in which we rank at the top in the world. The future of higher education will increasingly be defined by global collaboration. Whether addressing advances in artificial intelligence, health care, water resources and sustainability, or semiconductor manufacturing, universities must work together to prepare the next generation of leaders and solve challenges that no single institution or nation can address alone. That spirit of collaboration is central to our vision at the University of Arizona.Moving to live in another country is an exercise in learning and in adapting. Every institution has its own culture and expectations, but I quickly discovered that curiosity and integrity with a sense of purpose transcend borders. My education at IIT Madras and before, as well as at Ohio State and at the University of California Berkeley, gave me an outstanding technical foundation, and perhaps more importantly, it instilled discipline and a lifelong commitment to learning. Those lessons have stayed with me throughout my career. I have also been fortunate to work alongside exceptional mentors, colleagues and students from many different backgrounds. Those experiences have reinforced my belief that universities are strongest when they bring together people with diverse perspectives in pursuit of shared goals. Some of our greatest innovations, and our greatest opportunities, come through learning from one another.IIT Madras challenged us to think critically and take on complexity with confidence. It taught us to remain curious and continue learning throughout our lives. It was a hyper-competitive atmosphere, but perhaps that helped me discover my core strengths and built resilience. My training prepared me well for graduate study in the United States, and it shaped my approach to leadership. Whether in research or university administration, progress begins with asking the right questions and listening carefully. Bringing together talented people with different perspectives is invaluable. The challenges facing higher education, and society more broadly, are increasingly complex. Solving them requires institutions that are willing to innovate, partner strategically and remain focused on uplifting society.Artificial intelligence offers a generational opportunity. As chair of the US Department of Energy’s Genesis AI Mission advisory subcommittee, I would like to emphasize the opportunity and the challenge. Like every transformative technology, AI presents challenges that must be addressed thoughtfully, but it also has tremendous potential to accelerate discovery, improve teaching and prepare students for a rapidly changing workforce. Our responsibility is to help students think critically, apply these technologies ethically and develop the creativity, judgment and leadership that remain uniquely human. Throughout history, universities have helped society navigate periods of profound change. AI is no different. Public research universities have both the opportunity and the responsibility to ensure these technologies are developed and applied with humanity at the core.My research and teaching career has fundamentally shaped how I approach leadership. Engineers are trained to ask questions, rely on evidence and solve complex problems collaboratively. Those same habits are invaluable in leading a university. Although I spend less time directly conducting research today, remaining engaged with our faculty, students and research enterprise keeps me connected to the university's core mission. Great public research universities create opportunity. They prepare students to lead, advance discoveries that improve lives and serve as engines of economic growth and societal progress. At the University of Arizona, success for every student is our North Star. My responsibility is to help create an environment where students, faculty and staff can thrive, where discovery translates into opportunity and where our work uplifts the people of Arizona and communities around the world.I also enjoy staying connected with cutting-edge research in my roles providing strategic research leadership through advisory committees for the National Science Foundation, US Department of Energy, and Sandia National Laboratories among others.India will always be an important part of who I am. I remain connected through family, lifelong friendships, professional colleagues and the global IIT alumni community. Those relationships continue to be an important part of my personal and professional life. I also value opportunities to remain engaged with higher education leaders across India, including through my role as Chair of the Global Advisory Council for the Confederation of Indian Private Universities. I maintain a longstanding commitment to strengthening collaboration between universities in India and the United States and creating opportunities for institutions to learn from one another.As Arizona’s flagship, land-grant university, we believe our responsibility extends beyond our campus. We are committed to building partnerships that expand educational opportunity, strengthen research and create meaningful impact for the communities we serve. I believe India’s universities will play an increasingly important role in shaping the future of higher education, and I look forward to strengthening those relationships in the years ahead.I am deeply proud of what our university community has achieved together. Since coming to the University of Arizona, we have restored financial stability by eliminating the university’s $177 million budget deficit while continuing to invest in our people and keeping resident undergraduate tuition flat for three consecutive years to preserve access and affordability.We implemented a new enrolment management strategy that creates multiple pathways to the university while investing in the academic and well-being programs students need to graduate in four years with minimal debt and pursue strong career opportunities. That commitment includes making counselling services available to students at no cost, removing a financial barrier to care and helping ensure students have the support they need to thrive. We are equally committed to preparing students to succeed in an increasingly interconnected world. One example is the expansion of our Study Abroad program, made possible by a generous $20 million gift from the Garcia Family Foundation. This investment will provide international experiences to students who otherwise might not have had the opportunity to study abroad, broadening their perspectives and better preparing them to lead in a global economy. We continue to build momentum. Our responsibility is to serve as a force for good for Arizona and beyond. That is the work that inspires me every day.
Article Summary: Suresh Garimella is the President of the University of Arizona. He earned his bachelor’s degree from the Indian Institute of Technology Madras. In an exclusive interview with Ishani Duttagupta, he discusses his deep connection with the global IIT alumni network, the contribution of Indian students to his university.

Article Title: FSSAI flags GLP-1 food claims, cracks down on rotten food, pesticide-tainted raisins
Article Text:
FSSAI cracks down on misleading 'healthy food' claims, tightens noose on brands

NEW DELHI: A nutrition product promoted for people undergoing GLP-1/GIP therapy, loose raisins carrying unsafe pesticide residues and expired or rotten food sold through Flipkart have all landed on the radar of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ), which has initiated separate enforcement action in the three cases.FSSAI has issued a notice to Dr Reddy’s and Nestle Health Science Ltd, Tirupati Wellness Pvt Ltd, Flipkart India Pvt Ltd, Amazon Seller Services Pvt Ltd and Netmeds Healthcare Ltd over non-compliant advertising and claims for Celevida GLP+ on e-commerce platforms.Among the claims flagged by the regulator was that the product provided “high protein support for lean muscle preservation during GLP-1/GIP therapies”. FSSAI also flagged claims such as “helps maintain lean muscle”, “supports muscle strength” and “preserve lean mass” and questioned the use of the brand name “Celevida GLP+” along with therapy-related claims, saying this could create a misleading association between the product and such therapies.The regulator further objected to descriptions including “complete daily nourishment” and “dependable nutrition in every serving”, saying these could portray the product as a complete nutrition product or meal replacement.A representation that it was “imported from Europe for purity” was also found misleading, as European origin by itself does not establish enhanced or superior protein quality.FSSAI also flagged the claim “Contains 100% RDA BCAA” as misleading and directed food businesses to discontinue use of “100%” on food labels, packaging and promotional material. It also said the disclaimer that “Celevida GLP+” was merely a brand name did not offset the misleading impression created by the overall presentation, while claims on muscle strength, immunity support and energy metabolism were also found potentially misleading.In the raisins case, FSSAI has sanctioned prosecution against Nex International after a regulatory sample of loose raisins was found unsafe. The company appealed against the Food Analyst’s report, following which the counterpart sample was sent to a referral laboratory. The referral laboratory confirmed the sample was unsafe, with pesticide residues including carbendazim and lambda-cyhalothrin.FSSAI has meanwhile suspended with immediate effect the licence of Shreyash Retail Pvt Ltd, a Flipkart seller, after receiving over 130 complaints, including more than 70 about expired or rotten food. Inspections of Flipkart facilities in Delhi and Noida also found expired and near-expiry products and hygiene deficiencies. In some cases, consumers reported vomiting after consuming expired food.According to Amazon spokesperson, Amazon.in operates as an online marketplace where independent third-party sellers list and sell their products. We require sellers to list products which comply with applicable Indian laws and Amazon policies. We remove noncompliant product listings upon directions from relevant regulatory authorities. We confirm that the said product is no longer available on our marketplace.
Article Summary: FSSAI has issued a notice to Dr Reddy’s and Nestle Health Science Ltd, Tirupati Wellness Pvt. Ltd, Flipkart India Pvt Ltd, Amazon Seller Services Pvt and Netmeds Healthcare Ltd over non-compliant advertising and claims for Celevida GLP+ on e-commerce platforms. The regulator has sanctioned prosecution against Nex International after a regulatory sample of loose raisins was found unsafe. In some cases, consumers reported vomiting after consuming expired food.

Article Title: India to come out with a national plan to boost small-scale fisheries sector
Article Text:
India already has policies and schemes covering several aspects of small-scale fisheries. The NPOA-SSF is intended to bring these strands together into a single, measurable and participatory national framework, with clearly identified priorities, responsibilities, resources and monitoring mechanisms.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The government is preparing to come out with a National Plan of Action on small-scale fisheries to promote the sector in a coordinated manner, keeping an eye on the country’s target to scale up its seafood exports to Rs 1 lakh crore by 2030. The livelihood of about 30 million fisherfolk is linked to fisheries and allied activities in India.As part of the exercise, the department of fisheries has sought fishers’ views before framing the plan, whose draft is expected to be released around World Fisheries Day on Nov 21, and has written to coastal states and UTs to designate a nodal officer or team, organise stakeholder consultations this month and share the feedback with a dedicated national task force which will prepare the draft.India already has policies and schemes covering several aspects of small-scale fisheries. The NPOA-SSF is intended to bring these strands together into a single, measurable and participatory national framework, with clearly identified priorities, responsibilities, resources and monitoring mechanisms.The National Plan of Action on small-scale fisheries (NPOA-SSF) is being developed in line with the voluntary guidelines for securing sustainable small-scale fisheries of the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and India’s national policy on marine fisheries, 2017.“The plan will address a broad range of issues affecting small-scale fishing communities, including access to fisheries resources, sustainable fisheries management, gender equality, climate change and disaster risk,” said P Krishnan, director, Bay of Bengal Programme Inter-Governmental Organisation (BOBP-IGO).The BOBP-IGO is facilitating and coordinating the exercise as the Centre requested coastal states and UTs to conduct their own state-level consultations and consolidate fishers’ views for framing the plan.As part of strengthening the sector, the govt last year released a national framework to establish a centralised digital traceability system for fisheries and aquaculture to ensure compliance with international regulations, promote food safety and improve market access.The move is expected to help India expand its export markets for fisheries in the wake of the imposition of high tariffs by the US on Indian shrimp and other marine products. India’s seafood exports amounted to Rs 62,408 crore in 2024-25, with a substantial amount of it coming from shrimp exports.Since the framework for the centralised digital traceability system will facilitate enhanced transparency and robust quality assurance, the marine commodity can easily be accepted in other markets, as it will enable real-time, end-to-end tracking of seafood products from ‘farm to plate’ and ‘catch to consumer’ — an essential requirement in many countries.
Article Summary: The livelihood of about 30 million fisherfolk is linked to fisheries and allied activities in India. India already has policies and schemes covering several aspects of small-scale fisheries. The NPOA-SSF is intended to bring these strands together into a single, measurable and participatory national framework.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

In 2024, Tom Brady used his platform to support Floridians facing the aftermath of Hurricane Milton, making a $100,000 donation toward disaster relief. The initiative aimed to get basic supplies into the hands of people dealing with the storm’s immediate impact, while supporting broader recovery efforts across Florida.Brady announced his contribution shortly after Hurricane Milton struck Florida as a powerful Category 3 storm. The hurricane brought dangerous winds, storm surge and heavy rain, while tornadoes added another layer of risk across parts of the state.The storm left millions of customers without electricity and caused widespread damage. With communities facing urgent shortages, Brady focused his donation on practical necessities rather than simply offering public support."In the wake of Hurricane Milton, I'll be making a donation of $100k to help get essentials like food, water and first aid to fellow Floridians in need," Brady posted on X.His contribution also opened the door for people who wanted to help but could only give smaller amounts.GoPuff, which had partnered with Brady earlier that year, agreed to match donations made through its Give With Gopuff programme."My friends at @gopuff are matching this, along with all other donations made via 'Give With Gopuff', all benefiting the Volunteer Florida Foundation," Brady said. "Keep those impacted by these storms in your prayers, look out for your neighbors, and continue to help out anyway you're able. Stay safe, and stay strong Florida."The GoPuff campaign gave users a direct way to donate everyday essentials through the company's app. For each eligible item donated through the Give With Gopuff collection, the company pledged to match the contribution and send the products to the Volunteer Florida Foundation, up to $1 million.GoPuff also committed additional bulk donations through the Florida Disaster Fund to help supply relief centres across the state.Brady was not the only major name to step forward after Milton. Taylor Swift also announced a significant contribution to hurricane recovery efforts. Feeding America said the singer donated $5 million to support people affected by Hurricanes Helene and Milton."We’re incredibly grateful to Taylor Swift for her generous $5 million donation to Hurricanes Helene and Milton relief efforts,” Feeding America's CEO Claire Babineaux-Fontenot wrote. “This contribution will help communities rebuild and recover, providing essential food, clean water, and supplies to people affected by these devastating storms."Together, the donations from Brady, Swift and other contributors highlighted the scale of the response needed as Florida communities began the difficult process of recovery.
Article Summary: Tom Brady donates $100,000 to Hurricane Milton relief. GoPuff and Taylor Swift also support hurricane victims. Brady announced his contribution shortly after Hurricane Milton struck Florida. Taylor Swift donated $5 million to support people affected by Hurricanes Helene and Milton.

Article Title: Retail dal prices surge by Rs 20-30 a kg across Mumbai Metropolitan Region
Article Text:
Pulse prices at the wholesale market rose by an average of Rs 15 from the previous month because of tight local supplies.





NAVI MUMBAI: Prices of major pulses have risen by Rs 10-20 per kg in Vashi APMC wholesale market in recent weeks amid supply shortages, deficient monsoon rainfall, drought conditions, higher logistics costs and festive demand. Retail prices have increased by Rs 20-30 per kg.Pulse prices at the wholesale market rose by an average of Rs 15 from the previous month because of tight local supplies.Grain, Rice and Oilseeds Merchants’ Association (GROMA) president Bhimji Bhanushali said lower food grain arrivals followed drought conditions across Maharashtra. Wholesale price increases were being reflected in retail markets, where restrictions were limited, he said. Rohan Sawant, a consumer, said the recent hike in prices has disturbed the kitchen budget badly. Wholesale chana prices climbed from Rs 72 to Rs 82 per kg over the past month, while retail prices increased from Rs 110 to Rs 130. Tur prices rose from Rs 90 to Rs 105 per kg at APMC, while retail tur dal averaged about Rs 150 per kg, up from Rs 120 in Mumbai Metropolitan Region. Wholesale moong dal prices increased from Rs 95 to Rs 105 per kg, while retail prices averaged Rs 140.A wholesaler said prices could continue rising because of production losses in growing regions across Maharashtra and elsewhere in the country. Bhanushali said major pulse-producing states received below-average rainfall during the June-Sept monsoon, prompting drought declarations in parts of Karnataka and Maharashtra. Millers and stockists had also increased inventories before the festive season, while annual increases in minimum support prices affected selling prices. APMC grain market director Nilesh Veera said premium Kolam rice prices had risen from Rs 50 to Rs 60 per kg over the past fortnight, while basmati rice prices were also affected. Basmati rice prices rose by an average of Rs 5 per kg, while wheat and millet prices remained unchanged. Veera said govt was considering reducing import duty on pulses to stabilise the local market, but its impact was yet to be seen.
Article Summary: Pulse prices at the wholesale market rose by an average of Rs 15 from the previous month because of tight local supplies. Wholesale chana prices climbed from Rs 72 to Rs 82 per kg over the past month. Tur prices rose from Rs 90 to Rs 105 per kg at APMC, while retail tur dal prices, up from Rs 120 in Mumbai Metropolitan Region.
